Behavior change: fetch_blocks_from_peers now returns as soon as no request is in flight, instead of idling until the 4s FETCH_FROM_PEERS_TIMEOUT. This affects two cases: no request was sent because every selected block was already locked, or the last outstanding request failed with no peer left to retry on. In both cases no further network request is sent, and a failed request still waits the full 2s request timeout, so periodic runs cannot repeat faster than every ~2s on failures. The only new cost is local: while all selected blocks are locked, the scheduler polls get_missing_blocks at its default 200ms cadence instead of every 4s, which is the same cadence it already uses during fast successful sync. items.excerpt: For 11 years, a Massachusetts man had an alarming array of health problems, most notably that his heart kept failing. He landed in the hospital over and over again, needed life support at one point, spent years going to specialists, and underwent a barrage of tests along the way. But through it all, he never revealed a key detail behind his ailments: He was taking powerful, illicit synthetic testosterone derivatives (aka anabolic-androgenic steroids, or AAS). One of the drugs he took was approved only for use in animals; it's primarily used to beef up cows. Left in the dark, his doctors had to puzzle this out on their own. In a case report in this week's issue of the New England Journal of Medicine, they explain how they did it. They also offer a warning: These cases will only become more common, and clinicians need to know what they look like. Read full article Comments
items.title: Man's secret use of synthetic testosterone for cows nearly destroyed his heart

items.excerpt: Abstract PropAMMs are on-chain venues whose prices are set by a single maker. The maker pushes quote state on-chain, and fills read that state. We decoded 92,627 fills on nine Ethereum PropAMMs over 30 days (10 September to 9 October 2026) from execution data. We priced the 69,827 WETH/stablecoin fills against Binance one-second trades. Three of the registry venues accept maker state only if it is stamped with the current block’s timestamp. Their fills always execute against an update in the same block. Takers pay about 0.45 bp at the fill, on every one of the 30 days. Over the following five minutes the price does not move in their favour on average, in any taker class: there is no sign of adverse selection. Of fills after a CEX move of more than 0.5 bp in the preceding 12 seconds, 78.5% trade against it. The PropAMM quote follows the CEX in the same block, while Uniswap lags. items.excerpt: One nice thing about discovering exoplanets is that, once you work out how long their orbits take, they continue to show up like clockwork. The timing is so regular, in fact, that we can use variations to detect the gravitational influence of additional planets in the same exosolar system. And the precise timing is useful in that we can rely on it to point telescopes at the system when we know some of the light we detect has passed through the planet's atmosphere. Except when we can't. On Monday, researchers reported on an exoplanet that simply stopped showing up. TOI-2535b is a hot Jupiter-sized planet we've been observing as it transits between its host star, TOI-2535, and Earth for about seven years now. But it recently stopped showing up, and researchers suspect that's due to an unseen companion orbiting in a different plane. Read full article Comments

Kubernetes schedules pods individually and independently, but distributed training introduces two requirements that break this model: Pods must land on hardware with the right inter-GPU bandwidth, and all pods must be scheduled simultaneously. Topology-aware scheduling (TAS) and gang scheduling address these two requirements and help organizations extract full value from GPU capacity, which represents a growing share of infrastructure spend. TAS shapes the relative placement of pods to enable fast communication between GPUs. Gang scheduling helps ensure that all pods in a distributed job start running simultaneously, preventing the partial starts that leave GPUs allocated but idle. QuePaxa is an unusual choice; most consensus systems use well-established consensus algorithms like Raft, (Multi-)Paxos or Viewstamped Replication. items.excerpt: Even my family thinks I’m a little robotic. Logical, linear, sequential, methodical. But hey, I’m an engineer, and that’s part of what makes me good at my job. If I were operating on the same volatile cocktail of emotions, knee-jerk reactions, and intuition that most people operate on, I wouldn’t have been nearly as effective building enterprise software architecture at Disney, Dell, SAP, VMware, and now Control Plane. Worse yet, I might have had to become a marketer, or a designer, or a human resources specialist…or even a salesperson. items.excerpt: We made a design decision in stacks-passkey-wallet that’s worth putting in front of this forum: the wallet is derived from the passkey rather than stored anywhere. The path: WebAuthn PRF output → HKDF → BIP-39 entropy → Stacks and Bitcoin keys. A pure function, so the same passkey always yields the same keys, and they’re re-derived each time they’re needed. The seed phrase is still fully available to the user: they can reveal it, write it down, and restore in any standard Stacks wallet. The honest limit: a key derived on demand in a browser session is hot-wallet-class security, and we treat it that way. The library is MIT, open source, with two separate kinds of evidence: 81/81 on its internal suite, and 43/43 plus 5 negative controls on an independent vector verifier that imports nothing from the library.
